This is Mika. She lives in Ishinomaki. At six forty-one, her biggest problem was the toaster.
At six forty-two, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck off the coast of Miyagi. Her phone already had a statement ready.
Three minutes later came a tsunami warning, and a helpful note about her insurance.
Mika joined the walk to higher ground. Her phone offered her an upgrade.
At the shelter, the power went out. Her phone, on four percent, suggested a candle subscription.
On day two, rescue teams arrived from the United States, along with a form. Mika started page one of six hundred.
That evening, another aftershock. A subcommittee met to decide whether it set a precedent. Mika reached page two hundred.
On day four, the trains came back, and so did Mika. The toast was exactly where she left it.
